Lighthouse Radio: Stay Off Air
Every Thursday she called in with a fake voice. Tonight she uses her own.
A late-night host falls for the anonymous caller in the lighthouse. The hard part isn't meeting her. It's keeping her off the air.

For a year, Wren has closed The Late Light with a Thursday caller who used a voice changer and hung up first. Tonight Ada calls with her real voice and asks Wren not to play the song, just to wait. Now Wren has a lighthouse keeper who wants to be known by one person, a sponsor who wants a love story, and a folder of recordings that isn't hers to use. You decide how a woman who talks for a living learns to keep something quiet.
The show's adult night producer, who runs the board, screens the calls, and knows exactly which light is line two.
If nobody acts, Ada's voice becomes a segment, and the one person who called because she could hang up first stops calling at all.

Stop the on-air questions before they start

Mic in the Car

No recording. No audience.

You Said Breakfast

Behind the WCLP station, the parking lot
